title: The Water Shortage That Revealed Midway
text:
In the spring of 1942 US Navy codebreakers at Station Hypo in Pearl Harbor, led by Commander Joseph Rochefort, were reading parts of the main Japanese naval code. They could see that Japan was preparing a major operation against a target referred to as AF. Rochefort's team believed AF was Midway Atoll, but others in Washington thought it might be somewhere else, such as Hawaii, the Aleutians or the US west coast. Admiral Chester Nimitz, with only a few carriers left, needed to know where to place them.

To settle the question, the codebreakers devised a test. The garrison on Midway was instructed, through a secure undersea cable, to send a radio message in plain language reporting that its water distillation plant had broken down. Soon afterward the codebreakers read a Japanese message reporting that AF was short of water.

With the target confirmed, and with further decrypts indicating the timing, Nimitz placed his three carriers northeast of Midway, waiting for the Japanese fleet. On 4 June 1942 American aircraft fatally damaged four Japanese fleet carriers, the core of the force that had attacked Pearl Harbor, while the Americans lost the carrier Yorktown. Japan's naval offensive in the Pacific never recovered.
lesson: When you are unsure what someone's words mean, design a small test that forces the answer. Confirming one key fact can change how you deploy everything else.
people: Joseph Rochefort, Chester Nimitz, Edwin Layton, Jasper Holmes
location: Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, and Midway Atoll (USA)
source: Edwin T. Layton, And I Was There (1985); W. J. Holmes, Double-Edged Secrets (1979); Gordon Prange, Miracle at Midway (1982)
